handoff.head: 80456c7dcec03b6a9ad40c81fce47c9e8d99b366
handoff.conclusion: Toolroll now cleans up after itself. Suites run in their own process group and temp root, and both are removed on pass, fail, timeout or interrupt. The worker runs a daily storage sweep claimed in SQLite. It removes stale test temp folders and stops orphaned run processes, revalidating each before signalling. It also removes finished checkouts, staged runtimes beyond current/previous/newest, and dependency installs unused for 7 days. Spotlight markers are added. toolroll storage and Settings > Storage show the last sweep.
changes: New: scripts/suite-lifecycle.mjs, src/storage-sweep.ts, src/orphan-sweep.ts, src/staged-runtimes.ts, src/never-index.ts; storage_sweep table added without a version bump (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS)
Release-check checkouts now go once complete unless deployed now or the project's newest complete gate with no deploy since, for at most a week; the old 7-day per-release keep is gone
deploy-browser prunes staged runtimes through the shared module: current, previous and newest only (it kept the 3 newest before); with no runtime in use it removes none
Spotlight markers go in the pool and project folders, not inside checkouts, so builds can't commit them; also deps root, linked node_modules, staged-upgrades and temp roots
verification: npm run typecheck passed; 14 focused test files, 160 tests passed, incl. a subprocess suite test (pass/fail/timeout/SIGINT) and a real Vitest run interrupted mid-test
Headless Storage journey on the built candidate at 1280 and 390 wide (empty/normal/long/failure): no overflow, Details opens by keyboard, 44px tap target on phone, no page errors
Full release verifier not run here (left to the machine gate)
followUps: Proof/canary scripts that keep their output on purpose (crash/pilot/handoff canaries, screenshot proofs) still leave temp folders; the daily sweep removes them after a day
Unit tests and e2e workers set TOOLROLL_STORAGE_SWEEP=off so a test never sweeps the host; production workers sweep by default
Orphan detection needs lsof on macOS or /proc on Linux; if it can't read them, it stops nothing and the sweep records the failure and retries in an hour

handoff.conclusion: Batch checks added, off by default per project (project checks --batch on|off, Settings → Projects → Checks). handoff.conclusion: Project identity no longer hashes st.dev (path, real git common dir, inode, birth time); every caller goes through learningIdentity. Stale knowledge never fails a build: it runs without it, the brief says it was not applied, and an approver applies it forward from the Knowledge page or toolroll knowledge apply as a new revision, recorded in an append-only project_identity_carry table. Rows under the old formula with the current st.dev carry over silently; a repo recreated at the same path still asks.
changes: project-learning.ts: identityOf/legacyIdentityOf, carryProject, reconcileIdentity, acceptedIdentities; learning checks accept carried identities, writes use the current one.
project-knowledge.ts: stale knowledge is shown for review only, never applied; applySavedKnowledge (refuses the lead); snapshots of stale builds are stored under the current identity.
project-skills.ts, coding-handoff.ts, coding-context.ts accept carried identities; a skills freeze proceeds without skills saved under an un-carried identity.

Console: one notice, saved knowledge in a disclosure, Apply saved knowledge button (action=apply, CSRF, approver). CLI: knowledge apply in knowledge-cli.ts, operate.ts and surface.ts (operator audience).
Chat: conversationKnowledge returns the stale notice with the Knowledge page path and the CLI command instead of throwing.
verification: npm run typecheck passes.
npx vitest run on project-learning, project-knowledge, project-skills, coding-context, project-delete, operate and pull-request-flow test files: all pass.
followUps: Chat gap: chat cannot apply stale knowledge itself; it points to the Knowledge page and the CLI command.
Skills saved under an un-carried identity still raise an error on the Skills page; applying knowledge records the carry, which clears it.
verifyCodingContext has no store, so it accepts only the current or same-volume legacy identity, not approver carries.
The shared node_modules was unreadable from this worktree, so I ran a private npm install here (package files unchanged).
